author: polymorph
text:
I'm with you Josh, not really sure. I hoped my pic of the NU would spark some discussion and clarification but hasn't really yet. I clearly see a flag of sideways movement and thought there would be limits (FL) on each side of that as I labeled it and as the line graph shows in the FL section of Marketpedia.

What I really don't get is regardless of what we call them (FL, FTR, Cap, etc.), what difference does it make? Do we trade them differently? It seems like the first time that price returns to any of them they are traded the same way. If that's true, do we need different names for them? If that's not true, what is the difference? In case there's any confusion, that's not an attack on the material, names, etc., just the truth: my brain has yet to clearly comprehend what those things are or the differences between them.

Someone here (DrSwing or Les_Paul, I think) suggested practicing what you know and trusting more would come (or some similar sentiment), so that's what I'm doing. I don't know the names but the Source of the Engulf (wanna call it SOE in the meantime?) seems to be a big deal. Tell me what you (or anyone else) think of the chart below - it's the same NU M15 that I posted yesterday and you commented on today. It is updated using my current understanding: the zone where price starts its move to ENG a high of resistance, low of support, or zone of supply or demand is a big deal and can be traded the FTB and maybe on subsequent returns too. I also posted in my journalusing the same methodology on an AU D1 chart. I invite all to comment, correct, and clarify both here and there. As always, thanks in advance!
